title: Snubbers and Thrust Restraints
description: FanPedia's snubber and thrust restraint drawings (p. 135): an isolation base with snubbers and a detail inset, and a fan-to-duct joint with two thrust restraints, with nine numbered markers, leader lines and label strips. Explore mode previews each part's name and description; quiz mode hides the labels and describes each part by its job or place, with two attempts, a hint after the first miss and mastery at 8 of 9 on the first attempt.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Parts of a snubber and a thrust restraint on a spring-isolated fan
learningObjectives: The learner will identify the nine labeled parts of a snubber on an isolation base and of a thrust restraint across a fan-to-duct joint, given each part's function or location.
prerequisites: open, housed, restrained and seismic springs

accessibility.notes: The drawing is a labelled SVG group; every numbered marker is a focusable role=button and Tab walks them in number order; Enter or Space selects one; focus or hover previews its name and description. During the quiz the markers are named only 'Part n' until resolved, labels and leader lines are hidden, and hints never name the answer. Verdicts and prompts are announced through FP.announce (aria-live). ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and an 'Answer' badge pair with colour. Text is 12 px or larger; markers keep a constant pixel size; the label strips move below the drawing on narrow screens.

simulation.modelType: labeled diagram with locate quiz (FP.Overlay callout engine on FP.CalloutQuiz)
rules: Explore mode: hover or focus previews a part's name and description; click, Enter or Space opens it and counts it as visited; never scored.
Quiz mode: 9 prompts in a seeded shuffle (the same order for every learner; Start over reshuffles).
Two attempts per prompt; the first wrong answer shows a hint that does not name the answer; the second reveals the answer and counts as missed.
Selecting empty space uses no attempt.
Only first-attempt answers count toward mastery; mastery is 8 of 9.
assumptions: FanPedia p. 135 snubber and thrust restraint drawings, with the printed labels, colour legend and captions removed; marker positions are percentages of the image.
limitations: The drawings are FanPedia's, not a specific current catalog model; only one of the two thrust restraints carries markers, and the isolators marker sits on one of the several isolators on the base.

sources: FanPedia p. 135 (Vibration Isolation: Isolator Types; snubbers on an isolation base with a detail inset, and thrust restraints): drawing, part names and the snubber description
FanPedia p. 197 (thrust restraints): ceiling hung type isolators, threaded rod, two restraints per fan mounted 180 degrees apart
Drawing: FanPedia, Twin City Fan, p. 135

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore labelled markers on the real FanPedia drawing first, then retrieval practice: find each part from a description of its job, with a hint after the first miss and immediate correction.
keyQuestions: Which part keeps the two snubber brackets from touching metal to metal?
Which parts of a thrust restraint stop a spring-mounted fan from moving horizontally at every start?
commonMisconceptions: A snubber holds the fan rigidly in place.
The snubber's two brackets touch when it engages.
The flex connector keeps a spring-mounted fan in place.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 9'; mastery is 8 of 9 on the first attempt.
